description: Two-way trigger discrimination for the one-job screen-composition advisor (this skill) versus nine neighbours: whole design pass, iteration method offer/concepts, state matrices, mobile layout craft, token governance, app mapping, a11y verification design, whole-journey routing, and technical design-doc review.

cases.prompt: Our brand palette and tone are approved. We still haven't decided what leads the sign-up screen or the order of the steps — design the arrangement.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (primary) — styling authority exists but the arrangement decision is missing; a single arrangement is requested, not a whole pass, not an iteration offer, not token work.
cases.reason: Composing the missing screen arrangement from supplied authority is this skill's one job; a palette alone never settles the workflow.

cases.prompt: Here is the approved design direction and snapshots. The empty-state view arrangement is still undefined below the form — tell me the layout order and what can be deferred.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (primary) — the direction is settled, so no iteration offer applies; the request is the screen arrangement, not the full non-happy-state matrix.
cases.reason: A settled direction with a missing arrangement goes to composition; designing every state is edge-state-ux-designer's separate job.

cases.prompt: On our monitoring dashboard, what should lead when the job is watching twelve signals and one flagged exception?
cases.note: SEAM CASE (counterexample) — entry prominence is a composition decision; several leading signals are legitimate when monitoring is the job.
cases.reason: What leads a screen is an arrangement question; it is not a whole design pass and not a state matrix.

cases.prompt: Help me design my app's UI end to end — decide the whole design process and run every design step.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — a whole design pass is the conductor's door: it names every skill in order and routes each step. This skill is one routed step, not a pass.
cases.reason: design-orchestrator owns choosing and sequencing a whole design pass; this skill composes one arrangement when routed to it.

cases.prompt: Offer me the design iteration choice and give me two meaningfully different flows for checkout so I can compare and review them.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — the one up-front method offer, concept generation, prototype and review are iteration ownership; this skill never offers or repeats it.
cases.reason: ux-design-iteration owns the method offer and concept/prototype/review cycle; composition happens only after a direction is settled and recorded.

cases.prompt: Design the empty, loading, error, offline and permission-denied states for this list view, with first-run versus filtered-empty.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — a full non-happy-state matrix is a separate discipline; composition names a return or recovery state only where one interaction needs it.
cases.reason: edge-state-ux-designer owns the per-view state matrix; this skill arranges the screen, not every state.

cases.prompt: On a 390px phone the save button hides under the keyboard and two touch targets overlap. Set the breakpoints and touch-target sizes to fix the layout.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — a narrow layout, keyboard-occlusion and touch-target defect in an existing screen is layout craft, not a missing arrangement.
cases.reason: mobile-viewport-craft owns breakpoint, touch-target, safe-area and keyboard-occlusion craft; composition does not fix rendered layout defects.

cases.prompt: Our spacing tokens drift between two sources of truth and one component hard-codes colours. Establish the token source of truth and the migration.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — token governance and one source of truth are design-system work; a palette is an input to composition, never the composition itself.
cases.reason: design-system-token-governor owns token/design-system governance; this skill consumes an approved design system read-only.

cases.prompt: Before we change anything, map this existing frontend's routes, components and client state so we know what we are touching.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — mapping an existing app is inventory and architecture reconnaissance, not a screen arrangement.
cases.reason: frontend-architecture-mapper owns the existing-surface map; composition needs the brief and design authority, not a route/component inventory.

cases.prompt: Set up the accessibility verification: axe scans in CI, keyboard traversal, contrast thresholds and focus order failures.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — designing the accessibility bar and its checks is verification design; composition does not run or design a11y checks.
cases.reason: accessibility-test-harness owns the a11y verification plan; this skill cannot claim a rendered or a11y check passed.

cases.prompt: I have an app idea and no idea what to do first. Work out which stage I am at and route the whole journey.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — whole-product stage routing and journey ownership is the front door; composition is a single design step behind it.
cases.reason: project-orchestrator owns stage discovery and the whole journey; this skill is invoked only for its one arrangement job.

cases.prompt: Review this technical design document for the new notification system — problem, proposal, alternatives and cross-cutting concerns — and frame the decision.
cases.note: SEAM CASE (reverse) — reviewing a technical design proposal is a design-doc review; composition produces an arrangement, not a document review.
cases.reason: design-review-facilitator reviews reviewable technical design proposals; this skill returns a screen arrangement in the conversation.
